clips.title: From zero to marathon in 18 months
clips.text: I had a client, Maria, who couldn't run for five minutes straight when we met. She was 42, worked night shifts, and hadn't exercised in a decade. We started with walk -run intervals, one minute jogging, two minutes walking, three times a week. Every two weeks we added a minute to the jog. No speed work, no fancy gadgets, just consistency. 18 months later, she crossed the finish line of the Chicago Marathon in 5 hours 12 minutes.

clips.title: Nothing new on race day
clips.text: Where do most people go wrong? They wait until race week to experiment. Your gut is a muscle. It needs training just like your quads, and it takes weeks to adapt to carbohydrate concentration. So you make them practice breakfast. Practice your race day breakfast on every single long run. Same oatmeal, same banana, same coffee, same timing. Never try anything new on race day. I had a runner who swore by a new caffeinated gel at mile 20. He'd never used it in training. At mile 22, he cramped so badly he walked the last 4K. Meanwhile, another athlete ate the exact same toast with peanut butter and honey she'd eaten before every 20 -miler for 12 weeks. She negative -split the marathon. Your stomach remembers, don't surprise it when the stakes are highest. That's a great rule, nothing new on race day period.
